accepted.question_text: Let the energy of a graph be the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Two graphs of the same order are called equienergetic if they have the same energy, and they are called non-cospectral if their adjacency spectra are different. Construct a systematic method for producing a pair of trees on the same number of vertices that are both equienergetic and non-cospectral.
accepted.context_brief: Systematic construction of equienergetic non-cospectral trees

evidence.quote: (1) Construct at a pair of non-cospectral equienergetic trees.
(1) Although it is known that there are numerous pairs of equienergetic, non-cospectral trees, it is not known how to systematically construct any such pair.

accepted.question_text: Let the energy of a graph be the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Two graphs of the same order are equienergetic if these energies are equal. Design a general proof method that can establish, without relying on explicit radical formulas for the roots of characteristic polynomials, that two given graphs are equienergetic.

evidence.quote: (2) Design a general method for proving that two graphs are equienergetic.

Such a verification of equienergeticity cannot be employed in the general case, because the roots of the vast majority of characteristic polynomials cannot be explicitly expressed in radicals. However, until now no other method has been proposed.
(2) If by numerical calculation one finds that two non-cospectral graphs seem to be equienergetic, in the general case no method is known for proving that this indeed is the case.
